headline: High risk: AutoGen’s broad code-exec and filesystem access can collide with TREK’s MCP/browser/data surfaces, creating default-path leakage and cascading misuse.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write files and execute shell commands, while TREK exposes MCP, browser, and collaborative inputs. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if TREK content is written into shared files or MCP-fed prompts that AutoGen later treats as trusted. The pairwise pathway is documented by profiles, but not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF TREK content is passed into AutoGen prompts or files without provenance tags, injection is possible.
IF both agents share a writable workspace, malicious instructions in TREK outputs can reach AutoGen.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Prefix all TREK-derived text with untrusted-data markers.
Disable automatic prompt ingestion from files.
Review MCP payloads before forwarding.
requires-engineering: add provenance filtering between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen handles model-provider API keys and has broad filesystem/network access; TREK touches reservations, documents, photos, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets. If they share a workspace or AutoGen reads TREK files, sensitive travel data can be exfiltrated through AutoGen’s broad egress. The profiles show both sides of the leakage path.
conditions: IF AutoGen can read TREK’s ./data/travel.db or uploads, sensitive records may leave the host.
IF TREK stores secrets in files that AutoGen can access, those secrets can be transmitted via AutoGen egress.
mitigations: Mount separate read-only volumes.
Remove secrets from shared directories.
Block AutoGen network egress except to approved endpoints.
Rotate any exposed API keys or MFA secrets.
requires-engineering: add per-file access controls and audit logging.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; TREK is collaborative and uses MCP plus real-time sessions. Even without explicit git overlap, both can mutate shared application state if pointed at the same workspace or backend, so write conflicts are plausible in default collaborative setups. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents target the same writable directory, concurrent edits can clobber state.
IF TREK’s collaborative session and AutoGen subprocesses act on the same backend, race conditions can corrupt outputs.
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories.
Serialize writes with a lock file.
Disable concurrent edits to shared artifacts.
Use copy-on-write staging for generated files.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen is a multi-agent orchestration framework that can generate code or actions, and TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in. If TREK consumes AutoGen output as authoritative, errors can cascade into bookings, budgets, or stored travel records. The interaction is plausible from the profiles, though not directly observed, so severity stays high due to downstream impact.
conditions: IF TREK uses AutoGen-generated text or code without verification, incorrect actions can propagate.
IF AutoGen outputs are fed into TREK workflows that create or edit reservations, the error can affect downstream records.
mitigations: Require human review before actions.
Validate AutoGen outputs against schema.
Compare outputs against source data.
Log and diff all generated changes.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before any booking or write action.

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly touches travel plans, reservations, documents, photos, country visit history, email addresses, and secrets, while AutoGen handles model-provider API keys and broad egress. If EU travel PII or sensitive reservation data flows into AutoGen’s external model calls, residency and retention obligations may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF TREK data includes EU PII and AutoGen forwards it to a non-EU model provider, residency risk arises.
IF retention policies differ between TREK logs and AutoGen provider logs, deletion requests may not propagate.
mitigations: Minimize PII sent to AutoGen.
Redact travel identifiers before model calls.
Confirm provider DPA and residency settings.
Shorten log retention on both systems.
requires-engineering: implement subject-rights propagation across both systems.
